result.summary:
Read analysis.md §5 (round 2, seed 802, group B) and its four literature topics L5-L8, targeting core A (intraday volume log-change, day_mean(in_logchg(Volume,60)) smoothed), core B (day_durbin_watson(High) convex aggregation), and core C (cross_quantile_q25(LogFloatShares,241), not recommended). Loaded WebSearch/WebFetch via ToolSearch and searched each topic, verifying publication dates via Crossref/IDEAS/NBER/arXiv (not just the year shown in search snippets).

L5 (mean vs. extreme-value aggregation for core B): Bali-Cakici-Whitelaw's MAX effect (JFE 2011) and Ang-Hodrick-Xing-Zhang IVOL (NBER 2004/JF 2006) give direct, dated support for trying cross_max/cross_quantile_q90 on day_durbin_watson(High) as a cheaper alternative to stacking convex powers; no literature found comparing "convex-then-mean" vs "direct max/quantile" aggregation specifically (gap, honestly noted).

L6 (intraday volume shape as a persistent stock characteristic, core A): found evidence the U-shape itself is non-stationary over time (Graczyk & Queirós 2018, arXiv) and execution-focused volume-forecasting papers (Markov et al. 2019), but no direct academic precedent treating a stock's own intraday volume shape as a persistent cross-sectional factor characteristic — same gap as round 1's L2/L4, reported honestly rather than papered over.

L7 (exclusion screens vs. linear combination for the cs_last_high* filter tasks): Lin et al. (2020, Pacific-Basin Finance Journal) is a direct precedent for excluding extreme-strength stocks from momentum portfolios (positive result). Han & Lesmond (2011, RFS) and Chen/Jiang/Xu/Yao (2020, J. Empirical Finance) give directly conflicting findings on whether screening out microstructure-noise-prone stocks removes noise or reveals real alpha in the idiosyncratic-vol anomaly — flagged as the key methodological lesson for task 4.2 #10. A breakpoint-sensitivity paper was found but its journal date (2023-12) is after the cutoff, so it was excluded per rules.

L8 (is core C's low-price family already a known, redundant anomaly?): Birru & Wang (2016, JFE; working paper Dec 2012) gives a belief-based (price-anchors-skewness-expectations) mechanism rather than a liquidity one. Bae/Bhattacharya/Kang/Rhee (2019, J. Financial Markets) shows nominal-price anchoring is global and actively maintained via stock splits, which argues against the "it will decay after 2015" rationale. A directly on-point China A-share paper (Bing Zhang, Int'l Review of Economics & Finance) was found but its Crossref online date is 2023-11 — after the 2023-08-08 cutoff — so it was excluded and explicitly logged as "found but date-disqualified," along with the point that the "known anomaly" framing for China A-shares currently rests on US-literature analogy rather than direct A-share evidence.

Wrote the full writeup (processing-method translations per topic, each tagged [S#]; honest gap/exclusion notes; a 13-row verified source table with title/authors/year-month/venue/link/verified; and a one-paragraph summary for the PI) to /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/research/coldstart_C05/partura/s802/r2/lit.md via the Write tool, confirmed on disk with ls -l (21165 bytes). No files outside the permitted read/write scope were touched, no code was run or modified, and no git actions were taken.
